instructions:
1. Wedge one end of a barbell into a landmine or a corner.
2. Stand to the side of the bar and grip the loaded end with the near hand.
3. Keep a slight bend in the elbow and brace your core.
4. Raise the bar out to the side until your arm reaches shoulder height.
5. Lower the bar under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbow, not the hand, to keep tension on the side delt.
2. Avoid shrugging the shoulder up toward the ear.
3. Use a slow, controlled tempo on the way down.
4. Keep the torso still and resist leaning toward the bar.

instructions:
1. Wedge one end of a barbell into a landmine and hold the loaded end at shoulder height.
2. Step back into a reverse lunge, lowering the back knee toward the floor.
3. Drive through the front foot to return to standing.
4. As you rise, press the bar overhead until the arm is extended.
5. Lower the bar back to the shoulder and reset.
6. Repeat, alternating legs.
tips:
1. Brace the core to resist the diagonal pull of the bar.
2. Time the press to finish as you reach standing.
3. Keep the front shin vertical during the lunge.
4. Move smoothly rather than rushing the transition.

instructions:
1. Wedge one end of a barbell into a landmine.
2. Lie back on a bench or the floor facing the bar and hold the loaded end with both hands.
3. Start with the arms extended over the chest.
4. Bend the elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead.
5. Extend the elbows to press the bar back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arms still and let only the forearms move.
2. Lower the bar under control to stretch the long head of the triceps.
3. Keep the wrists firm and neutral.
4. Brace the core to keep the torso stable.

instructions:
1. Wedge one end of a barbell into a landmine.
2. Stand facing the bar and hold the loaded end with both hands at chest height.
3. Extend the arms out in front and brace the core.
4. Rotate the bar down and across toward one hip.
5. Control the bar back up and across to the other hip.
6. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Drive the rotation from the trunk, not just the arms.
2. Pivot the feet slightly to protect the knees.
3. Move under control to resist the bar's momentum.
4. Keep the arms long and the elbows soft.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor and place a foam roller horizontally under your upper back.
2. Cross your arms over your chest and lift your hips off the floor.
3. Push through your feet to roll the roller slowly up and down the upper back.
4. Pause on any tight spot.
5. Lower your hips and reset.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Stay above the mid-back and do not roll over the lower spine.
2. Roll slowly and control the pressure with your feet.
3. Keep the core engaged to protect the neck and spine.
4. Breathe steadily and relax into each tender spot.
